In inferior temporal cortex and the visual areas of the superior temporal sulcus, by contrast, almost all neurons were contingent on the perceptual dominance of an effective stimulus, placing those areas beyond the resolution of the ambiguity.

items.question: In Dehaene and colleagues' 2001 fMRI study of masked words, which cortical areas did unseen masked words activate, and where did the activation disappear?
items.answer: Masked words activated left extrastriate, fusiform and precentral areas, and produced case-independent repetition suppression in the left fusiform gyrus. Compared with unmasked presentation the evoked activation was drastically reduced and was undetectable in prefrontal and parietal areas, matching the participants' inability to report the words.

items.question: In Sergent, Baillet and Dehaene's 2005 attentional-blink study, which early ERP components were preserved for unseen words, and at what latency did seen and unseen words diverge?
items.answer: The early P1 and N1 potentials were evoked intact by unseen words, which argues they are not the primary correlate of conscious perception. Brain responses to seen and unseen words diverged rapidly at around 270 ms, after which several events were evoked solely by seen words.

items.question: Two Dehaene-lab studies from 2005 and 2007 - one on the attentional blink, one on backward masking - converge on a latency. What are the numbers in each, and what is the masking threshold Del Cul et al. report?
items.answer: With backward masking, subjects fail to perceive the target unless the target-mask interval exceeds roughly 50 ms; subliminal processing was found early in the occipito-temporal pathway (under 250 ms), while the correlate of conscious reportability was a late, highly distributed fronto-parieto-temporal activation after about 270 ms. The attentional-blink study independently placed the divergence between seen and unseen words at around 270 ms. Both therefore locate conscious access in a late distributed wave rather than in early sensory potentials.

items.question: The P3 and induced gamma-band activity were long treated as signatures of visual awareness. What did Pitts and colleagues find in 2014 when they manipulated awareness and task relevance independently?
items.answer: Both induced gamma and the P3 were absent for task-irrelevant stimuli regardless of whether subjects were aware of them, and both were robust but dissociable for task-relevant stimuli. The authors concluded that gamma and the P3 reflect distinct post-perceptual processes needed to carry out the task, not conscious perception itself - so neither is a clean neural correlate of awareness.

items.question: Why did consciousness researchers start building no-report paradigms, according to Tsuchiya and colleagues' 2015 review?
items.answer: Because asking subjects to report what they experience biases the search for the neural correlates of consciousness: the measured activity mixes the substrate of experience with the machinery that enables reporting. No-report paradigms attempt to dissociate the two by studying conscious experience in the complete absence of any report, and the review argues that report-based and no-report designs are complementary rather than that either alone settles the question.

items.question: Frässle and colleagues used optokinetic nystagmus and pupil size to track binocular rivalry without asking for reports. What changed in the frontal cortex between the active-report and passive conditions?
items.answer: With active report, occipital, parietal and frontal areas all showed rivalry-related activity, replicating earlier findings. When observers experienced the same rivalry passively without reporting alternations, differential frontal activity was absent while occipital and parietal activation persisted. The authors took this to question the popular view that frontal areas drive perceptual alternations.

items.question: Man hör ofta att hjärnan stänger av när man somnar. Vad hittade Massimini och kollegor 2005 när de sköt in en TMS-puls i premotoriska barken under djupsömn och mätte svaret med tät-EEG?
items.answer: Tvärtom - det första svaret vid stimuleringsstället blev starkare under icke-REM-sömn än i vaket tillstånd, men det slocknade snabbt och spreds inte vidare bortom stimuleringsstället. I vaket tillstånd följdes ett initialt svar efter ungefär 15 millisekunder av en serie vågor som vandrade flera centimeter bort till anslutna barkområden. Poängen är alltså inte att hjärnan blir tyst, utan att den effektiva kopplingen mellan barkområden bryts.

items.question: Ferrarelli and colleagues extended the sleep TMS-EEG finding to a drug in 2010. Which drug, how long did the awake responses last, and what measure discriminated the two states?
items.answer: They used the benzodiazepine midazolam. During wakefulness TMS triggered responses in multiple cortical areas lasting more than 300 ms, whereas during midazolam-induced loss of consciousness the evoked activity was local and of shorter duration. A measure of how far the evoked cortical currents propagated - significant current scattering - reliably discriminated consciousness from loss of consciousness, mirroring what had been seen in early non-REM sleep.

items.question: How is the perturbational complexity index (PCI) computed in Casali et al. 2013, and which states was it tested across?
items.answer: PCI perturbs the cortex with transcranial magnetic stimulation to engage distributed interactions, then compresses the spatiotemporal pattern of the electrocortical response to measure its algorithmic complexity - integration and information in one number. It was tested on TMS-evoked potentials from healthy subjects in wakefulness, dreaming, non-REM sleep and sedation with midazolam, xenon and propofol, and on patients emerged from coma in vegetative state, minimally conscious state and locked-in syndrome, discriminating the level of consciousness in single individuals.

items.question: Är gränsvärdet för perturbationskomplexitetsindex (PCI) en universell mätare av medvetande? Vad gjorde Casarotto och kollegor 2016?
items.answer: Nej. Gränsvärdet togs fram empiriskt i en referenspopulation på 150 personer - friska och hjärnskadade som själva kunde bekräfta om de var medvetna eller inte - där det skilde medvetna från omedvetna tillstånd med 100 procents sensitivitet och specificitet. Först därefter användes samma gräns på patienter som inte kunde kommunicera: känsligheten blev 94,7 procent för minimalt medvetet tillstånd, och 9 av 43 patienter i vegetativt tillstånd hamnade över gränsen. Måttet är alltså kalibrerat mot en referensgrupp, inte en fristående medvetandemätare.

items.question: What problem with the original PCI did PCIst solve in 2019, on how many subjects was it validated, and what did the intracranial test show?
items.answer: The original PCI needed an elaborate setup and offline processing and applied only to TMS with high-density EEG. PCIst, based on dimensionality reduction and quantification of state transitions in the evoked potential, matched the original's accuracy while computing in under a second. It was validated on TMS/hd-EEG from 108 healthy subjects and 108 brain-injured patients, and on sparse intracranial recordings from 9 patients undergoing single-pulse electrical stimulation it quantified a systematic drop in intracranial complexity during sleep.

items.question: Vad visade Owen och kollegor i Science 2006 hos en patient som uppfyllde kriterierna för vegetativt tillstånd?
items.answer: Med funktionell magnetresonanstomografi bad de patienten föreställa sig att spela tennis respektive gå runt i sitt hem. Patienten aktiverade de förväntade barkområdena på ett sätt som inte gick att skilja från friska försökspersoners. Det gällde en enda patient, och fyndet tolkades som bevarad medveten varseblivning trots diagnosen.

items.question: Monti and colleagues scaled the tennis-imagery paradigm to a cohort in the NEJM in 2010. How many patients were studied, how many could wilfully modulate their brain activity, and how many communicated?
items.answer: 54 patients with disorders of consciousness were studied at Cambridge and Liege. Five were able to wilfully modulate their brain activity during the mental-imagery tasks; in three of those five, further bedside testing revealed some sign of awareness, while in two no voluntary behaviour could be detected clinically. One patient answered yes-or-no questions during fMRI, although no communication could be established at the bedside.

items.question: Cruse and colleagues moved covert command-following from fMRI to bedside EEG in 2011. How many of their vegetative-state patients responded, and how accurate was the classification?
items.answer: Of 16 patients diagnosed as vegetative, 3 (19 percent) could repeatedly and reliably generate appropriate EEG responses to two distinct motor-imagery commands despite being behaviourally entirely unresponsive, with classification accuracy of 61 to 78 percent. Twelve healthy controls were also tested, and no significant relation was found between the patients' clinical histories and their responses.

items.question: In Claassen et al. 2019, how often was brain activation to spoken motor commands detected in acutely unresponsive ICU patients, and how did those patients fare at 12 months?
items.answer: 16 of 104 unresponsive patients (15 percent) had brain activation detected by EEG at a median of 4 days after injury. Eight of those 16 (50 percent) improved enough to follow commands before discharge, versus 23 of 88 (26 percent) without activation. At 12 months, 7 of 16 (44 percent) with activation reached GOS-E level 4 or higher versus 12 of 84 (14 percent) without, an odds ratio of 4.6 (95 percent CI 1.2 to 17.1).

items.question: What proportion of participants without an observable response to commands showed cognitive motor dissociation in the 2024 NEJM multicentre cohort, and what was the comparable rate among participants who did respond behaviourally?
items.answer: Cognitive motor dissociation was detected in 60 of 241 participants without an observable response to commands, that is 25 percent, out of a total sample of 353 adults across six international centres. Among the 112 participants who did have an observable response to verbal commands, 43 (38 percent) showed a response on task-based fMRI or EEG. So roughly one in four unresponsive participants performed the task, versus about one in three responsive ones.

items.question: Popular coverage often suggests that unresponsive brain-injured patients are usually conscious inside and that the imaging test simply reveals it. What do the largest cohorts actually support?
items.answer: They support a minority, not a majority, and a test that misses people. Detection rates for covert command-following are about 15 percent in acute ICU patients (16 of 104) and 25 percent in the large chronic multicentre cohort (60 of 241). The paradigm also produces false negatives: in 50 intracerebral-haemorrhage patients who could follow or mimic commands behaviourally, those with impaired comprehension - receptive or global aphasia - were markedly less likely to show brain activation to the motor command (odds ratio 0.23, 95 percent CI 0.05 to 0.89). A negative result therefore does not establish absence of awareness, and a positive rate of one in four is not most patients.

items.question: Why did Claassen's group test aphasia in patients who could already follow commands, and what did the study quantify?
items.answer: Because a command-following paradigm depends on the patient understanding the command, occult aphasia is a candidate source of false-negative cognitive-motor-dissociation results. They prospectively studied 61 ICU patients with acute primary intracerebral haemorrhage who had behavioural command-following or could mimic commands; 50 completed both the aphasia battery and the EEG motor-command paradigm, and 72 percent (n=36) had aphasia. Patients with impaired comprehension were less likely to show brain activation (odds ratio 0.23, 95 percent CI 0.05 to 0.89, p=0.04).

items.question: Hur ofta blev diagnosen vegetativt tillstånd fel när Schnakers och kollegor 2009 jämförde läkarnas konsensusbedömning med den standardiserade skalan CRS-R?
items.answer: Av de 44 patienter som det medicinska teamet enats om var i vegetativt tillstånd befanns 18 (41 procent) vara i minimalt medvetet tillstånd enligt CRS-R. Av 41 patienter med konsensusdiagnosen minimalt medvetet tillstånd hade fyra (10 procent) redan tagit sig ur det. Studien omfattade 103 patienter, och slutsatsen var att andelen feldiagnoser inte hade minskat nämnvärt på 15 år.

items.question: Standardised assessment reduces misdiagnosis in disorders of consciousness - but how many CRS-R examinations does it take, and what is the error rate after just one?
items.answer: In 123 chronic patients each assessed at least six times within 10 days, the diagnosis based on a single CRS-R differed from the six-assessment reference diagnosis in 36 percent of cases, and diagnoses remained statistically different from the reference up to the fourth examination. The authors recommend at least five assessments within a short interval, for example two weeks. That is on top of the earlier finding that clinical consensus alone misclassified 41 percent of vegetative-state patients relative to a single CRS-R.

items.question: In the 2014 Lancet clinical validation study, how did FDG-PET and active fMRI compare for identifying minimally conscious patients?
items.answer: In 126 patients (41 unresponsive wakefulness syndrome, 4 locked-in, 81 minimally conscious), 18F-FDG PET had 93 percent sensitivity (95 percent CI 85 to 98) for identifying the minimally conscious state and 85 percent congruence with behavioural CRS-R scores. Active fMRI was substantially less sensitive at 45 percent (95 percent CI 30 to 61) with 63 percent congruence. PET was also the better outcome predictor at 12 months.

items.question: BIS-monitorn beskrivs ibland som en medvetandedetektor. Vad visade Avidans två stora randomiserade studier i New England Journal of Medicine 2008 och 2011?
items.answer: Ingen fördel för BIS. I studien från 2008 randomiserades 2000 patienter till BIS-styrd narkos (mål 40-60) eller styrning efter utandad narkosgaskoncentration, och det inträffade två säkra fall av vakenhet under narkos i vardera gruppen. I den större studien 2011 med 6041 högriskpatienter hade BIS-gruppen 7 säkra fall av 2861 mot 2 av 2852 i gasgruppen, och BIS-protokollets överlägsenhet kunde inte påvisas. Monitorn följer narkosdjup, inte medvetande som sådant.

items.question: The B-Aware trial is the one BIS study that did show a benefit. What was its effect size, and how large was the trial?
items.answer: In 2463 adults at high risk of awareness, there were 2 reports of awareness in the BIS-guided group (n=1225) versus 11 in the routine-care group (n=1238), p=0.022 - an 82 percent reduction in risk (95 percent CI 17 to 98 percent). The number needed to treat was 138, putting the cost of preventing one case at roughly 2200 dollars at the time.

items.question: What did the isolated forearm technique reveal about connected consciousness after tracheal intubation in the 2017 multicentre study, and did those patients remember anything?
items.answer: Of 260 adults, 4.6 percent (12 of 260) responded to a verbal command to move the isolated hand after intubation, and 5 of those 12 signalled pain through a second hand squeeze. None of the 253 patients questioned afterwards had explicit recall of intraoperative events. Depth-of-anaesthesia monitor values were higher in responders both before (54 plus/minus 20 versus 42 plus/minus 14) and after intubation (52 plus/minus 16 versus 43 plus/minus 16).

items.question: What incidence of connected consciousness after intubation was found in 18-to-40-year-olds, and how did it differ by sex?
items.answer: Responses after intubation occurred in 37 of 338 young adults, 11 percent. Females responded more often than males, 13 percent (31 of 232) versus 6 percent (6 of 106), with an adjusted odds ratio of 2.7 (95 percent CI 1.1 to 7.6). Continuous anaesthesia before laryngoscopy reduced the risk (adjusted odds ratio 0.43).

items.question: Varför skiljer sig ketamin från propofol och xenon när man mäter komplexiteten i barkens TMS-svar, och vad rapporterade försökspersonerna efteråt?
items.answer: Hos 18 friska försökspersoner gav propofol och xenon båda ett lågkomplext svar - ett lokalt aktiveringsmönster med låg amplitud vid propofol och en global, stereotyp långsam våg vid xenon - medan ketamin gav ett vaket-liknande, komplext mönster i tid och rum. Efteråt rapporterade ingen några upplevelser efter propofol eller xenon, medan ketamin gav långa, livfulla drömmar utan koppling till omgivningen. Oresponsivitet är alltså inte samma sak som medvetslöshet.

items.question: The spectral exponent of resting EEG was tested against the same three anaesthetics as the TMS complexity work. How many participants per drug, and how did ketamine behave?
items.answer: Five healthy participants per drug (xenon, propofol, ketamine) were dosed to unresponsiveness at Ramsay score 6. Loss of consciousness under xenon and propofol substantially steepened the power-spectral decay, making the negative broadband spectral exponent more negative in every subject. Ketamine instead kept an overall decay similar to wakefulness, consistent with preserved consciousness, but flattened the 20-40 Hz part. The exponent correlated highly with PCI.

items.question: Which three simultaneous EEG changes marked loss of consciousness during gradual propofol induction in Purdon et al. 2013?
items.answer: Loss of consciousness was marked simultaneously by an increase in low-frequency EEG power below 1 Hz, the loss of spatially coherent occipital alpha oscillations at 8-12 Hz, and the appearance of spatially coherent frontal alpha oscillations. These dynamics reversed on emergence, and the phase-amplitude relationship between the low-frequency and alpha rhythms predicted recovery of consciousness.

items.question: Schartner and colleagues measured MEG signal diversity under psilocybin, ketamine and LSD. How did the values compare with normal waking rest, and which measure showed it most strongly?
items.answer: All three psychedelics produced reliably higher spontaneous signal diversity than waking rest, even after controlling for spectral changes - the first time such measures exceeded normal waking values rather than falling below them as under propofol. The increase was most pronounced for single-channel Lempel-Ziv complexity, that is for temporal rather than spatial diversity, and the changes correlated selectively with reported intensity of the psychedelic experience.

items.question: Is the psychedelic state a 'higher' level of consciousness, and what does that question reveal about the levels framework itself?
items.answer: Bayne, Hohwy and Owen argue that the level-of-consciousness framework used for coma, absence seizures, anaesthesia and sleep is untenable and should be replaced by a multidimensional account of global states. Applied to psilocybin and LSD, the review of lab-based findings shows that some aspects of consciousness are enhanced while many functional capacities associated with consciousness are seriously compromised - so calling the psychedelic state 'higher' is inappropriate, and the fact that different aspects move in different directions is itself evidence against a unidimensional level-based view.

items.question: Vad hittade Siclari och kollegor 2017 när de jämförde uppvaknanden då försökspersoner mindes drömmar med uppvaknanden då de inte mindes något?
items.answer: Med tät-EEG fann de att drömrapporter - både i REM-sömn och i icke-REM-sömn - hängde ihop med lokalt minskad lågfrekvent aktivitet i bakre barkområden. Högfrekvent aktivitet i samma område följde det specifika dröminnehållet. Genom att övervaka denna bakre heta zon i realtid kunde de förutsäga om personen skulle rapportera en dröm eller inte vid uppvaknande ur icke-REM-sömn.

items.question: In Voss et al. 2009, which frequency band separated lucid dreaming from ordinary REM sleep, and where on the scalp was it strongest?
items.answer: Lucid dreaming showed REM-like power in delta and theta but higher-than-REM activity in the gamma band, with the difference between states peaking around 40 Hz. That 40 Hz power was strongest in frontal and frontolateral regions. Six trained volunteers signalled lucidity with a pattern of horizontal eye movements while 19-channel EEG was recorded, and coherence overall was similar to waking and higher than in REM sleep.

items.question: Two-way communication with a dreaming person was demonstrated in 2021. How many participants were tested, how many questions were answered correctly, and how many individuals produced those answers?
items.answer: Procedures for two-way communication during polysomnographically verified REM sleep were implemented in 36 individuals across four independent laboratory groups. Correctly answered questions were recorded on 29 occasions, produced by 6 of the individuals tested, using distinctive eye movements and selective facial-muscle contractions. The participants ranged from novices to frequent lucid dreamers and included one patient with narcolepsy.

items.question: Kouider et al. looked for the adult signature of conscious access in infants. How many infants, which ages, and how did the latency of the marker change with age?
items.answer: 80 infants aged 5, 12 and 15 months viewed masked faces at varying visibility while ERPs were recorded. All age groups showed a late slow wave with a nonlinear profile at the expected perceptual thresholds - the infant counterpart of the adult late nonlinear response at roughly 300 ms. The component shifted from a weak and delayed response starting around 900 ms in 5-month-olds to a more sustained and faster response around 750 ms in the older infants.

items.question: Vad talar för att en kråka kan ha sinnesmedvetande, trots att fågelhjärnan saknar en skiktad hjärnbark?
items.answer: Nieder och kollegor lät kråkor utföra en visuell upptäcktsuppgift och registrerade enskilda nervceller i pallium i framhjärnan. Cellernas aktivitet följde fåglarnas rapport om huruvida de såg stimulus eller inte, i ett tvåstegsförlopp där den första komponenten främst speglade den fysiska stimulusstyrkan och den senare förutsade fågelns perceptuella rapport. Slutsatsen är att grunden för sinnesmedvetande antingen fanns före däggdjuren eller uppstod separat i fågellinjen, och alltså inte nödvändigtvis kräver en hjärnbark.

items.question: What is the structural argument Barron and Klein make for subjective experience in insects, and how far back does it push the origin of consciousness?
items.answer: In vertebrates the capacity for subjective experience is supported by integrated midbrain structures that build an egocentric neural simulation of the mobile animal in space; Barron and Klein argue that structures in the insect brain perform analogous functions, so the insect brain also supports the most basic aspect of consciousness. The supporting structures are anatomically very different in the two clades but basal to each, which leads them to trace the origins of subjective experience to the Cambrian - the argument is functional and comparative, not a claim that insect and vertebrate brains are alike.

items.question: What is the front-versus-back-of-the-brain debate, and how was it staged in the Journal of Neuroscience in 2017?
items.answer: It is the dispute over whether the frontal cortex specifies the contents of consciousness or merely supports monitoring and reporting. The journal ran paired Dual Perspectives pieces: Boly, Massimini, Tsuchiya, Postle, Koch and Tononi reviewed clinical and neuroimaging evidence for the back of the cortex, while Odegaard, Knight and Lau replied that three common claims - that PFC lesions do not affect subjective perception, that PFC activity does not carry specific perceptual content, and that PFC involvement is only driven by the reporting task - are incompatible with the evidence unless one restricts attention to studies with limited sensitivity.

items.question: Contrastive analysis - comparing trials where a content is consciously perceived against trials where it is not - is the standard method for isolating an NCC. What did Aru and colleagues argue it actually delivers?
items.answer: They argued the contrast does not isolate the NCC proper, because the NCC is confounded with the prerequisites for conscious processing of that content and with its consequences. Previous results therefore cannot be read unequivocally as neural correlates of conscious experience, and the paper proposes experimental strategies for untangling the three. The methodology remains valid and valuable, but a correlate found this way is not thereby shown to constitute the experience.

items.question: The 2025 adversarial collaboration between integrated information theory and global neuronal workspace theory reported results from how many participants and which methods, and what did it find against each theory?
items.answer: 256 human participants viewed suprathreshold stimuli for variable durations while activity was recorded with fMRI, MEG and intracranial EEG, under a preregistered design agreed by proponents of both theories and a theory-neutral consortium. IIT was challenged by a lack of sustained synchronization within the posterior cortex, contradicting the claim that network connectivity specifies consciousness. GNWT was challenged by the general absence of ignition at stimulus offset and by limited representation of certain conscious dimensions in prefrontal cortex. Some predictions of each theory were nonetheless supported.

items.question: What did Pinto and colleagues find when they tested split-brain patients with confirmed complete callosotomy across the whole visual field, and how did they establish that the responses were conscious?
items.answer: The patients could not compare stimuli across visual half-fields, replicating independent hemispheric processing. But contrary to the textbook picture, across a wide variety of tasks they showed full awareness of stimulus presence and well above chance recognition of location, orientation and identity throughout the entire visual field, irrespective of whether they responded with the left hand, the right hand or verbally. Confidence ratings were used to identify conscious perception, and even on high-confidence trials response type did not affect performance - suggesting severing the callosum splits visual perception but does not create two conscious perceivers.

items.question: What is blindsight, and what is the main methodological worry Cowey raises about the evidence for it?
items.answer: Blindsight is the ability of patients with clinically blind field defects caused by damage to primary visual cortex to detect, localise and even discriminate visual stimuli they deny seeing - a paradigm case of implicit knowledge. Cowey's worry is that possible artefacts abound, far more than for implicit memory or deaf hearing and numb touch, and are still frequently ignored or dismissed, with the result that many genuine qualities of blindsight remain uncertain. He notes that with blindsight now established in monkeys, the physiological literature on V1 removal becomes directly relevant to the human condition.

items.question: Integrated information theory identifies the quantity of consciousness with the measure Phi. What formal objection was raised in 2019 about Phi for general physical systems?
items.answer: For Phi to serve as an observer-independent quantity of consciousness, there should be no alternative formulae for Phi consistent with IIT's axioms and no cases where Phi is ill-defined. The paper presents three ways in which Phi in its current formulation fails those standards, and discusses how the problem might be addressed. The objection is about the definition of the measure, not about whether integration matters empirically.

items.question: In the 2004 BMC Neuroscience paper that launched integrated information theory, which two phenomenological properties of consciousness motivate the claim that consciousness is the capacity to integrate information, and how is Phi defined?
items.answer: Differentiation (the availability of a very large number of conscious experiences) and integration (the unity of each such experience). Phi is the amount of causally effective information that can be integrated across the informational weakest link of a subset of elements, and a complex is a subset of elements with Phi>0 that is not part of a subset of higher Phi.

items.question: What is "qualia space (Q)" in Tononi's 2008 provisional manifesto, and how does a particular experience correspond to it?
items.answer: Q is a space in which each axis represents a possible state of the complex, each point is a probability distribution over its states, and arrows between points represent the informational relationships generated by causal mechanisms. The set of informational relationships within a complex constitutes a shape in Q that completely and univocally specifies a particular experience.

items.question: Vilka tre grundsatser (axiom) räknar den uppdaterade beskrivningen av integrerad informationsteori från 2012 upp, och vad säger uteslutningspostulatet?
items.answer: Information (varje upplevelse är en av många, alltså specifik), integration (varje upplevelse är en enda, alltså odelbar) och uteslutning (varje upplevelse är bestämd, avgränsad till vissa saker och med en viss hastighet och upplösning). Uteslutningspostulatet säger att bara maxvärden av integrerad information räknas: en mekanism pekar ut exakt en maximalt oreducerbar mängd av tidigare orsaker och framtida verkningar, ett så kallat begrepp.

items.question: What identity does IIT 3.0 (Oizumi, Albantakis and Tononi, 2014) assert between experience and physical structure, and what does it imply about functionally equivalent feed-forward systems?
items.answer: An experience is identical to a maximally irreducible conceptual structure (a MICS, a constellation of concepts in qualia space), and the set of elements generating it constitutes a complex; the MICS specifies the quality of an experience and integrated information Phi-Max its quantity. It follows that there can be true "zombies" — unconscious feed-forward systems that are functionally equivalent to conscious complexes.

items.question: IIT 4.0 was published in 2023, nine years after IIT 3.0 and seven after the 2016 Nature Reviews Neuroscience statement of the theory. Which specific developments does IIT 4.0 claim over the earlier formulations?
items.answer: IIT 4.0 claims a more accurate formulation of the axioms as postulates and mathematical expressions, the introduction of a unique measure of intrinsic information consistent with the postulates, and an explicit assessment of causal relations; fully unfolding a system's irreducible cause-effect power yields distinctions and relations that account for the quality of experience. IIT 3.0 had defined the quantity of experience as Phi-Max over a maximally irreducible conceptual structure, and the 2016 account had already framed the physical substrate of consciousness as a maximum of intrinsic cause-effect power.

items.question: The 2012 updated account of IIT names three axioms; Tononi and Koch's 2015 "Consciousness: here, there and everywhere?" names five. Which two are added?
items.answer: Intrinsic existence and composition. The 2015 list is intrinsic existence, composition, information, integration and exclusion, whereas the 2012 account works with information, integration and exclusion.

items.question: What does IIT predict about a digital computer that faithfully simulates a human brain, and how does that connect to IIT 3.0's claim about feed-forward systems?
items.answer: Tononi and Koch state that, in sharp contrast to widespread functionalist beliefs, IIT implies digital computers would experience next to nothing even if their behaviour were functionally equivalent to ours and they ran faithful simulations of the human brain; feed-forward networks, however complex, are not conscious, nor are aggregates such as groups of individuals or heaps of sand. This follows the IIT 3.0 result that there can be true "zombies", unconscious feed-forward systems functionally equivalent to conscious complexes.

items.question: Papers and press reports sometimes speak of measuring "the Phi of the brain". What do the sources actually support about computing Phi for a real neural system, and what is the clinically deployed number instead?
items.answer: Exhaustively searching for the minimum information partition, which IIT requires to quantify integrated information, has a computational cost that grows exponentially with system size, which is what makes IIT difficult to apply to real neural data. The index actually used at the bedside, the perturbational complexity index, is not Phi: it is a theory-driven proxy obtained by perturbing cortex with transcranial magnetic stimulation and compressing the spatiotemporal pattern of the electrocortical response to measure its algorithmic complexity.

items.question: In Baars's 2002 retrospective on global workspace theory, which three reasons does he give for the theory having had little impact when the evidence for the conscious access hypothesis was first described about two decades earlier?
items.answer: Consciousness was controversial; the evidence, though extensive, was indirect; and integrative theory was unfashionable.

items.question: Vilka tre iakttagelser menar Dehaene och Naccache (2001) att varje teori om medvetande måste kunna rymma?
items.answer: Att en betydande mängd bearbetning kan ske utan medvetande; att uppmärksamhet är en förutsättning för medvetande; och att medvetande krävs för vissa uppgifter, nämligen sådana som kräver att information hålls kvar över tid, nya kombinationer av operationer, eller att ett avsiktligt beteende startas spontant.

items.question: In Sergent, Baillet and Dehaene's 2005 attentional-blink study, which early evoked potentials were intact for unseen words, and at what latency did the seen and unseen conditions diverge?
items.answer: P1 and N1 were evoked intact by unseen words, suggesting these are not the primary correlates of conscious perception. A rapid divergence was observed around 270 ms, after which several brain events were evoked solely by seen words; the abstract describes this as a late wave of activation spreading through a distributed network of cortical association areas rather than naming it the P3b.

items.question: Combining Del Cul, Baillet and Dehaene (2007) with Sergent, Baillet and Dehaene (2005): what masking threshold and what two timing windows do the global-workspace ERP studies report?
items.answer: In backward masking, subjects fail to perceive the target unless the target–mask stimulus onset asynchrony exceeds a threshold of about 50 ms. Del Cul et al. separate a considerable amount of subliminal processing early in the occipito-temporal pathway (under 250 ms) from a late (over 270 ms), highly distributed fronto-parieto-temporal activation that correlates with conscious reportability, which matches the divergence around 270 ms that Sergent et al. found in the attentional blink.

items.question: Dehaene and Changeux's 2011 Neuron review names three objective neural measures of conscious access. What are they?
items.answer: Late amplification of relevant sensory activity; long-distance cortico-cortical synchronization at beta and gamma frequencies; and "ignition" of a large-scale prefronto-parietal network.

items.question: How does the 2020 Neuron statement of the global neuronal workspace hypothesis describe what happens in the conscious state, and how does that relate to the 2011 characterisation of ignition?
items.answer: Mashour, Roelfsema, Changeux and Dehaene propose that in the conscious state a non-linear network ignition associated with recurrent processing amplifies and sustains a neural representation, allowing the corresponding information to be globally accessed by local processors. This is the same ignition that the 2011 review lists as one of three objective measures of conscious access, alongside late amplification of sensory activity and long-distance beta and gamma synchronization.

items.question: Where does Baars's 2005 chapter say the global workspace or "blackboard" architecture came from, and what imaging contrast does he cite as supporting it?
items.answer: The architecture comes from the cognitive architecture tradition in cognitive science, where Newell and co-workers first showed the utility of a global workspace or blackboard among distributed knowledge sources. Functional imaging shows conscious cognition associated with widespread cortical activity, notably toward frontoparietal and medial temporal regions, whereas unconscious comparison conditions activate only local regions such as visual projection areas; frontoparietal hypometabolism is implicated in deep sleep, coma, vegetative states, epileptic loss of consciousness and general anaesthesia.

items.question: Which two major criticisms of higher-order theories do Lau and Rosenthal explicitly defend against in their 2011 review of the empirical evidence?
items.answer: That prefrontal activity reflects attention but not awareness, and that prefrontal lesion does not abolish awareness.

items.question: Brown, Lau and LeDoux (2019) place higher-order theory relative to two rival families and reject one common equation. Which family does HOT sit between, and does HOT equate consciousness with metacognition?
items.answer: HOT is presented as an intermediate position between global workspace theory and early sensory views such as first-order local recurrency theories. Most proponents of HOT do not stipulate consciousness as equivalent to metacognition or confidence, and although higher-order states are cognitively assembled, the requirements are considerably less than often presumed — which is their answer to the charge of overintellectualising consciousness. The 2011 review by Lau and Rosenthal had earlier argued the higher-order view is testable and empirically supported against first-order, global workspace and recurrent visual processing alternatives.

items.question: In LeDoux and Brown's 2017 higher-order theory of emotional consciousness, what role do subcortical circuits play in conscious feelings?
items.answer: Subcortical circuits are not directly responsible for conscious feelings; they provide nonconscious inputs that coalesce with other neural signals in the cognitive assembly of conscious emotional experiences. Conscious experiences, regardless of content, arise from one general cortical network of cognition, so what differs between emotional and non-emotional states is the kind of input that network processes.

items.question: The 2017 Journal of Neuroscience "Dual Perspectives" pair on whether the neural correlates of consciousness lie in the front or the back of cortex is often cited as evidence settling the prefrontal question. What kind of papers are they, and what does each side claim?
items.answer: Both are Perspective pieces reviewing existing literature, not new decisive experiments. Boly, Massimini, Tsuchiya, Postle, Koch and Tononi critically review clinical and neuroimaging evidence for front versus back involvement in specifying conscious contents; Odegaard, Knight and Lau address three claims they call misconceptions — that prefrontal lesions do not affect subjective perception, that prefrontal activity does not reflect specific perceptual content, and that prefrontal involvement is solely driven by the need to make reports — arguing these are incompatible with empirical findings unless one restricts attention to methods with limited sensitivity.

items.question: What is the central analogy of attention schema theory as Graziano and Webb state it in 2015, and what testable prediction do they draw from it?
items.answer: The brain constructs a schematic, simplified model of the process of attention — the "attention schema" — in much the same way it constructs a schematic model of the body, the body schema, and the content of that model leads a brain to conclude it has a subjective experience. The prediction is that without awareness, attention should still be possible but should suffer deficits in control.

items.question: I de sex experiment som Wilterson med kollegor publicerade 2020 för att pröva uppmärksamhetsschemateorin — vad hände med utifrånstyrd respektive inifrånstyrd uppmärksamhet när försökspersonerna saknade medvetenhet om ledtråden?
items.answer: När deltagarna inte var medvetna om att ledtråden förutsade målet fanns båda effekterna kvar. När de däremot inte hade någon synupplevelse av själva ledtråden fanns den utifrånstyrda effekten kvar medan den inifrånstyrda försämrades. Ytterligare två experiment visade att en inlärd omedveten uppmärksamhetsförskjutning spred sig från tränade platser till intilliggande otränade platser. Detta stämmer med förutsägelsen från 2015 att uppmärksamhet utan medvetenhet fortfarande är möjlig men får sämre styrning.

items.question: Graziano's 2020 reply article sets out attention schema theory as a chain of four distinct things. What are they?
items.answer: What the brain actually, physically has; what is represented by information models constructed in the brain; what higher cognition thinks based on access to those models; and what the speech machinery claims based on the information within higher cognition. The claim to have an essentially magical, subjective mind is explained by the impoverishment and reduction of information along that pathway.

items.question: What does Graziano's 2022 PNAS framework add to attention schema theory beyond the mechanistic account, and what evidential claim does it make?
items.answer: It adds an evolutionary account, proposing how consciousness may have evolved over millions of years from fish to humans by emphasising the specific adaptive roles consciousness plays in cognition and behaviour. The evidential claim is that over the preceding several years a growing body of behavioural, brain-imaging and computational-modelling evidence has addressed aspects of the theory; the paper positions itself as an overarching framework rather than a report of new data.

items.question: Vad säger Lamme och Roelfsema (2000) om den framåtriktade vågen i synsystemet jämfört med återkopplande bearbetning?
items.answer: Den framåtriktade vågen grupperar snabbt sådana särdragsmönster som är fast inbyggda i synhjärnan, men kan förmodligen inte i sig ge upphov till en synupplevelse. I många fall krävs återkopplande bearbetning — via förbindelser inom områden och återkoppling från högre områden — innan ett föremåls särdrag grupperas uppmärksamt och stimulus kan nå medvetandet.

items.question: Lamme's 2006 paper argues for a methodological change in how consciousness is defined. What is the change, and what does he say it costs us?
items.answer: Rather than treating introspective or behavioural observation as the gold standard to which neural measures must be fitted, neural and behavioural measures should be put on an equal footing. The cost is that we must let go of our intuitive or psychological notions of conscious experience and move our notion of mind toward that of brain — he illustrates this with the visual case where neural and behavioural arguments converge on a definition of visual consciousness, building on the feedforward-versus-recurrent distinction he and Roelfsema drew in 2000.

items.question: Vilka två teorier riktar sig "uppvecklingsargumentet" (the unfolding argument) från 2019 mot, vilket gemensamt antagande angriper det, och vad blir slutsatsen?
items.answer: Integrerad informationsteori och teorin om återkopplande bearbetning, som båda kallas orsaksstrukturteorier. Det gemensamma antagandet är att rent framåtriktade system aldrig är medvetna och att återkopplande system alltid är det. Med satser från beräkningsteorin drar Doerig och medförfattare slutsatsen att sådana teorier antingen är falska eller ligger utanför vetenskapens område.

items.question: Does the unfolding argument settle whether integrated information theory is falsifiable? What does Hanson and Walker's 2021 formalisation show?
items.answer: No — the verdict depends on the level of abstraction chosen. Using isomorphic digital circuits with and without feedback, realizable with table-top electronics, they show IIT is simultaneously falsified at the finite-state-automaton level and unfalsifiable at the combinatorial-state-automaton level. Their general criterion is that to avoid being either already falsified or unfalsifiable, a scientific theory of consciousness must be invariant with respect to changes that leave the inference procedure fixed at a particular level in a computational hierarchy.

items.question: What is the "dissociative epiphenomenalism" charge that Herzog, Schurger and Doerig level at IIT in 2022, and why do they call it self-undermining?
items.answer: They argue IIT's consciousness is by construction fully dissociated from anything measurable, so IIT implies that both the level and the content of consciousness are epiphenomenal with no causal power — meaning we could not even trust reports about first-person experiences. Since such reports are what IIT takes as ground truth and the foundation of its axioms, accepting IIT leads to rejecting its own axioms. They also argue pure first-person experience cannot serve as a scientific foundation because it is not measurable except through reports, brain activity, and the relationship between them.

items.question: What did Doerig, Schurger and Herzog actually do in the 2021 "Hard criteria for empirical theories of consciousness" paper, and what problem motivated it?
items.answer: The motivating problem is that consciousness hosts far more competing theories than other fields of natural science, which they attribute to a lack of stringent criteria specifying how empirical data constrains theories. They argue consciousness is a well-defined topic from an empirical point of view, present a checklist of criteria empirical theories must cope with, and then review 13 of the most influential theories against that checklist.

items.question: Den motsatsställda samarbetsstudien som publicerades i Nature 2025 beskrivs ofta som att den avgjorde striden mellan integrerad informationsteori och global neuronal arbetsyta. Vad kom den faktiskt fram till?
items.answer: Ingen av teorierna bekräftades. Med 256 deltagare och mätningar med magnetkamera, magnetencefalografi och elektroder inne i hjärnan stämde resultaten med vissa förutsägelser från båda teorierna men utmanade samtidigt centrala antaganden hos båda. Integrerad informationsteori träffades av att ihållande synkronisering saknades inom bakre hjärnbarken, vilket motsäger påståendet att nätverkets kopplingar avgör medvetandet. Arbetsytemodellen träffades av att den förutsagda tändningen vid stimulusslut i allmänhet uteblev och av att vissa medvetna dimensioner var svagt representerade i pannloben; författarna påpekar att invändningarna även träffar andra teorier som delar dessa förutsägelser.

items.question: What did the 2023 PLOS ONE adversarial collaboration protocol preregister before any data were collected, and how many laboratories were to run it?
items.answer: Two experiments testing contrasting predictions of global neuronal workspace theory and integrated information theory concerning the location and timing of correlates of visual consciousness, with the predictions endorsed by the theories' own proponents and the expected outcomes specified in advance as supporting, refuting or challenging each theory. Six theory-impartial laboratories were to follow the protocol using fMRI, M-EEG and iEEG, with built-in replications both between labs and within datasets.

items.question: What participant numbers does the IIT-versus-GNWT adversarial collaboration report across its main paper and its two published data descriptors?
items.answer: The 2025 Nature report gives n = 256 human participants across fMRI, MEG and iEEG combined. The separately published data descriptors give N = 118 for the multi-site fMRI dataset and 38 patients undergoing intracranial monitoring across three research centres for the iEEG dataset.

items.question: The adversarial collaboration was extended to animals in a 2026 protocol. Which species, which recording method, and which causal manipulations are specified?
items.answer: Non-human primates and mice, viewing or listening to suprathreshold visual and auditory stimuli of variable duration in a go/no-go task that controls for report confounds, with neuronal responses recorded by Neuropixels electrodes from visual, auditory, posterior parietal and/or prefrontal cortical areas. Predictions about timing and location are tested causally by electrical stimulation of prefrontal regions in non-human primates and optogenetic silencing in mice.

items.question: Contrastive analysis compares conditions where a content is consciously experienced against conditions where it is not. Why does that not isolate the neural correlate of consciousness, and do no-report paradigms fix it?
items.answer: Aru, Bachmann, Singer and Melloni argue the contrastive comparison does not reveal exclusively the NCC, because the NCC proper is confounded with prerequisites for and consequences of conscious processing of that content, so previous results cannot be unequivocally interpreted as neural correlates of conscious experience. Tsuchiya, Wilke, Frässle and Lamme separately argue that the report requirement itself has biased the search over decades — but they state no-report paradigms have their own disadvantages and that report-based and no-report paradigms jointly, not no-report alone, bring us closer to the true neural basis.

items.question: Where does the 2016 Nature Reviews Neuroscience review place the anatomical neural correlates of consciousness, and why is that localisation contested rather than settled?
items.answer: Koch, Massimini, Boly and Tononi locate the anatomical NCC primarily to a posterior cortical hot zone including sensory areas, rather than to a fronto-parietal network involved in task monitoring and reporting, and note that some candidate neurophysiological markers of consciousness have proved illusory while measures of differentiation and integration are more promising. It is contested because Odegaard, Knight and Lau argue in the same period that prefrontal cortex is essential to subjective experience and that the claim that prefrontal involvement is driven only by report demands is incompatible with the empirical findings unless one restricts attention to insensitive methods.

items.question: What evidence from sleep does Siclari et al. (2017) contribute to the posterior hot zone proposal, and how well did it predict dreaming?
items.answer: Using high-density EEG and contrasting presence against absence of dreaming, reports of dream experience in both NREM and REM sleep were associated with local decreases in low-frequency activity in posterior cortical regions, and high-frequency activity in those regions correlated with specific dream contents. Monitoring this posterior hot zone in real time predicted whether an individual reported dreaming or the absence of dream experiences during NREM sleep, which supports the localisation the 2016 review had proposed.

items.question: Perturbationskomplexitetsindex (PCI) beskrivs som ett teoridrivet mått på medvetandenivå. Vad visade valideringen från 2016, och vad får man inte läsa in i de nio patienterna i vegetativt tillstånd som hamnade över gränsvärdet?
items.answer: Gränsvärdet togs fram i en jämförelsegrupp på 150 friska och hjärnskadade personer som själva kunde rapportera, där det skilde medvetna från omedvetna tillstånd med 100 procents känslighet och specificitet, och det gav 94,7 procents känslighet för minimalt medvetet tillstånd. Nio av 43 patienter i vegetativt tillstånd låg över gränsen. Sammanfattningen tolkar dem som att de kan ha en förmåga till medvetande som inte syns i beteendet — inte som ett bevis för att de var medvetna.

items.question: According to Friston's 2010 review, which single quantity keeps emerging as the thing being optimized when different global brain theories are read through the free-energy lens?
items.answer: Value — expected reward or expected utility — or its complement, surprise, that is prediction error or expected cost. The free-energy principle accounts for action, perception and learning, and Friston argues that several global brain theories, including neural Darwinism, information theory and optimal control theory, might be unified within a free-energy framework by this shared theme of optimization.

items.question: Vad innebär "interoceptiv prediktiv kodning" i den modell som Seth och Critchley föreslog 2013?
items.answer: Att den bayesianska hjärnhypotesen utvidgas till interoception, alltså sinnet för kroppens inre fysiologiska tillstånd, så att ramverket rymmer varseblivning, tänkande och handling tillsammans med kroppens egna signaler. Modellen medför en ny syn på känslor som interoceptiv slutledning och sägs kunna förklara en rad psykiatriska tillstånd som rör jaget.

items.question: What is the "beast machine" view of selfhood, and what mechanism does the earlier Seth and Friston paper give it?
items.answer: Seth and Tsakiris describe embodied selfhood as "instrumental interoceptive inference", emphasising allostatic regulation and physiological integrity, which accounts for its non-object-like character and its subjective stability over time and implies, contrary to Descartes, that experiences of embodied selfhood arise because of and not in spite of our nature as beast machines. The mechanism comes from Seth and Friston's account of interoceptive inference, in which bodily states are regulated by autonomic reflexes enslaved by descending predictions from deep generative models of our internal and external milieu, with precision or uncertainty translating into neuromodulation.

items.question: Seth and Hohwy (2021) argue for theories "for" consciousness science rather than theories "of" consciousness. What is the distinction and what motivates it?
items.answer: They object that the theories under discussion monolithically identify consciousness with some other phenomenon, process or mechanism, and that treating consciousness as a single explanatory target makes it hard to account for the diverse properties conscious experiences exhibit. Progress instead requires elaborating systematic mappings between physical and biological mechanisms and the functional and, crucially, phenomenological properties of consciousness — an approach for which they nominate predictive processing as a highly promising candidate.

items.question: The sensorimotor and enactive traditions both published statements in 2001. What does each say the neural correlate approach gets wrong?
items.answer: O'Regan and Noë argue that seeing is a way of acting rather than the activation of an internal representation: the outside world serves as its own external representation and the experience of seeing occurs when the organism masters the governing laws of sensorimotor contingency, with support drawn from sensorimotor adaptation, filling-in, visual stability across eye movements, change blindness, sensory substitution and colour perception. Thompson and Varela argue the substrates should be mapped at the level of large-scale, emergent and transient dynamical patterns rather than particular circuits or cell classes, and that standard NCC work wrongly assumes a one-way causal-explanatory relation, where their approach allows a two-way relationship between embodied conscious states and local neuronal activity.

items.question: Which four theoretical approaches does the 2022 Nature Reviews Neuroscience review by Seth and Bayne cover, and what does it say about whether they can be told apart?
items.answer: Higher-order theories, global workspace theories, re-entry and predictive processing theories, and integrated information theory. The review states it is unclear how current theories relate to each other or whether they can be empirically distinguished at all, describes each by which aspects of consciousness it explains, its neurobiological commitments and the data adduced for it, and outlines three ways theories must be developed to deliver a mature regimen of theory-testing.

items.question: How does the 2023 "Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence" report propose to assess whether an AI system is conscious, and which theories does it draw on?
items.answer: It derives "indicator properties" of consciousness from the best-supported neuroscientific theories, elucidated in computational terms so that existing AI systems can be assessed against them in detail. The theories surveyed are recurrent processing theory, global workspace theory, higher-order theories, predictive processing and attention schema theory; several recent AI systems are then assessed for those indicator properties.

items.question: Is there a peer-reviewed paper in the indexed literature that establishes integrated information theory as pseudoscience?
items.answer: No such finding appears in the indexed abstracts; the "pseudoscience" charge circulated as an open letter rather than as an empirical result, and where the label is discussed in the indexed literature it is resisted. Ruan and Li's 2024 analysis states explicitly that the problems of IIT are far from being "pseudoscience", attributing the criticism to a gap between two levels of explanation in the theory — an autonomous-systems or critical-complexity level and a level that claims to anchor consciousness strictly — with IIT's panpsychist tendency playing a crucial role.
